sections.html:
Nashua sits in southern New Hampshire, in southeastern Hillsborough County, and shares the county seat role with Manchester. Population is 92,435, and the city covers 31.73 square miles, of which 30.83 are land. The Massachusetts line is close, which shapes who shops and who buys here. South Nashua's commercial district, anchored by Pheasant Lane Mall, draws Massachusetts shoppers because New Hampshire has no sales tax.

The city grew from textile mills into financial and professional services, high technology and defense. BAE Systems, Dell and Oracle have operations here, and two medical centers, Southern New Hampshire Medical Center and St. Joseph Hospital, serve the area.

Nashua is usually described by district, and each has a different housing feel. These come up most when owners describe where a house sits:

  • Downtown, centered on Main Street, the oldest commercial district
  • The Tree Streets, a neighborhood near downtown reached by the Broad Street Parkway
  • The Millyard, the former mill district and the Nashua Manufacturing Company Historic District
  • French Hill, the northern area once called Nashville
  • The Amherst Street corridor (NH 101A) in the northwest
  • South Nashua, near the Massachusetts line

If your house is in or beside a historic district, ask the city what review applies before you plan exterior work as a pre-sale fix.

Nashua's 2025 tax rate is $16.83 per $1,000 of valuation, up 93 cents, or 5.83 percent, from the year before.

The tax year runs April 1 to March 31. The first bill is due July 1 and is estimated at half of the prior year's rate. The second bill is due once the state sets the new rate, generally no later than December 20. The abatement deadline is March 1.

Nashua prorates property taxes by the day from April 1 when a home is bought or sold. Your closing agent will work out the figure and show it on the settlement statement.

If you sold the property but still receive a bill, forward it to the current owner, or return it in the envelope with a note giving the sale date and the buyer's name. A new owner may see the old name for a while, since the Registry of Deeds has to send the transfer to the Assessor's Office. Taxes can be looked up online through the city's property tax self-service portal, which is a quick way to confirm that nothing is owed before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: How to challenge a Nashua assessment
sections.html:
Ask the Assessor's Office, at 603-589-3040, to review the data, then file a written abatement application by March 1. If you miss March 1, no action can be taken for the current tax year. You may still ask for a spring review, in which the Assessing Department may look at your value for the following tax year.

State rules set the rest of the path. The city has until July 1 to respond, and an appeal to the Board of Tax and Land Appeals or superior court, not both, is due by September 1. The abatement does not stop collection, so pay the bill. A homeowner planning to sell should decide early whether the effort is worth it, since a buyer will care more about future bills than a past refund.

The New Hampshire transfer tax is $.75 per $100 of the price, charged to each of the buyer and the seller under RSA 78-B. It is filed through Granite Tax Connect.

For a one to four family home, the seller must disclose in writing the private water and sewage systems, insulation, any federally designated flood hazard zone and any underground heating oil tank, under RSA 477:4-d. Ask the title company what other charges will appear at closing, such as a mortgage payoff or any unpaid tax.

sections.h2: Winter, water and the buyer's inspection
sections.html:
Nashua has cold winters and wet springs, so a buyer's inspector will usually look at:

  • Roof condition after snow and ice
  • Basement moisture and lot drainage
  • Heating equipment and fuel storage
  • Insulation, which the state disclosure form asks about

Fixing small items before listing can help a financed sale hold together. If you would rather not spend the time or money, a cash buyer who takes the house as-is removes most of that list from the negotiation.

The Everett Turnpike is the main highway, and U.S. 3 follows it from the Massachusetts border to Exit 7E. NH 101A (Amherst Street), NH 111 (Hollis Street), NH 111A and NH 130 (Broad Street) also serve the city. The Broad Street Parkway, completed in 2015, connects Exit 6 to downtown.

The Nashua Transit System operates nine bus routes, and Boston Express runs from the Nashua Transit Center, near Exit 8, to South Station and Logan Airport. Nashua Airport (Boire Field) handles general aviation only, so air travelers use Manchester-Boston Regional or Logan. Commuter rail to Boston is only a proposal, so do not count on it when you price a house.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Nashua
sections.html:
A cash sale in Nashua means you describe the house, receive an offer and choose whether to accept, without repairs or a lender appraisal. The steps that remain are the title search, tax proration and the state transfer tax.

Plan on three things before closing: a current tax payoff or confirmation that nothing is owed, your mortgage payoff if you have one, and a decision about what stays in the house. Once those are settled, the closing date is yours to pick within the title company's schedule.

faqs.q: What is the Nashua tax rate for 2025?
faqs.a: It is $16.83 per $1,000 of valuation, up from $15.90 in 2024.

faqs.q: When are Nashua property tax bills due?
faqs.a: The first bill is due July 1 and is based on half of the prior year's rate. The second is due after the state sets the rate, generally no later than December 20.

faqs.q: Are Nashua property taxes prorated when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxes are prorated by day from April 1 for a home that is bought or sold. Your closing agent will show the figure.

faqs.q: What if I missed the March 1 abatement deadline in Nashua?
faqs.a: No action can be taken for that tax year. You may request a spring review, which may lead to a review of your value for the following year.

faqs.q: Is there a sales tax or transfer tax on a Nashua house sale?
faqs.a: New Hampshire has a real estate transfer tax of $.75 per $100 on each of the buyer and the seller. The state has no general sales tax.
